body:
## Why
The [current finding contract](https://github.com/grove/gapline/blob/main/gapline-audit/SKILL.md) already requires precise evidence, counterevidence, uncertainty, and the smallest useful next action. In practice, the final action could still be too vague for a developer to confirm or dismiss the concern. We should improve **actionability**, not simply add report fields.

**Evidence gate:** look at real-host and independently reviewed findings from [#4](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/4) and [#5](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/5) to identify examples where a more discriminating follow-up would reduce developer work.

## Proposed approach
- For each sufficiently consequential **SUPPORTED** finding or **HYPOTHESIS**, propose the smallest observation or controlled experiment that can distinguish the concern from plausible counterevidence, where meaningful and safe to describe.
- Specify relevant setup/trigger, expected and alternative outcomes, observable signal, assumptions, and scope **when these matter**. Do not force a rigid form for straightforward source/document contradictions, no-finding reports, or unknown contracts.
- Distinguish proposed checks from performed tests: executable tasks remain **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. An audit itself remains read-only and must not silently call tests, builds, external services, or sibling projects.
- Preserve authoritative source of requirements and full observable contract (identity, ordering, side effects, exact bytes where relevant). Do not assert a reproduction from source-only reasoning.
- Compare old and new finding examples with independent reviewers: is the next action clearer, cheaper, falsifiable, and less likely to send the developer in the wrong direction?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Include contrasting examples: actionable uncertainty, direct documentation contradiction, legitimate alternative, and insufficient requirement context.
- [ ] Follow-up tasks include a discriminating observation where possible, plus an explicit **NOT RUN** label for executable experiments.
- [ ] Independent review finds improved or equal actionability without misleading certainty or unacceptable verbosity/cost; report negative results.
- [ ] Keep the default report short (up to three findings) and avoid mandatory new schema or workflow steps.
- [ ] Revise the shipped skill/reference and evaluation cases only after documenting the expected improvement.

## Out of scope
Running probes, generating patches, opening issues automatically, or mandatory Proofline/Faultline integration.
title: [P1] Make consequential Gapline findings verification-ready
